one_liner: Manage Loudoun County's review of legislative land development applications (rezonings, special exceptions) and coordinate with applicants, stakeholders, and decision-makers.
fit_summary: Daniel's policy knowledge, public-facing skills, and IEM government-client consulting fit the stakeholder and legislative-process side of this role. However, it is a professional planning position that likely expects land use planning education or experience, which Daniel's known background does not show. The posting text is brief, so the full qualifications on the county site will decide how big the gap is.
eligibility: Open to the public (local government): no federal status, clearance, or veterans' preference issue is stated in the posting.
Check the full posting for minimum qualifications; planner roles at this salary often require a degree in planning or a related field plus several years of land use experience.
Confirm whether AICP certification is required or preferred.
The posting says the role leads teams; verify whether supervisory experience is expected.
strategy: Read the full posting at the governmentjobs.com link for required education, years of experience, and supplemental questions before investing time; this summary omits them.

Frame your IEM work in terms of managing review or deliverable processes for government clients, coordinating multiple stakeholders, and working on deadlines, using only duties you actually performed.
Emphasize your strengths with public meetings, elected officials, and policy, since legislative applications go before the Planning Commission and Board of Supervisors.
Learn the basics of Loudoun's Zoning Ordinance, 2019 General Plan, and the rezoning and special exception process so your cover letter and supplemental answers sound credible.

Apply promptly because the closing date is not stated and county postings may close once enough qualified applicants apply. Local resumes are not bound by the federal two-page limit, but keep yours focused.
If you lack planning credentials, also apply to Planner I/II or planning technician roles in Loudoun, Prince William, or Fairfax as an entry path.
resume_bullets: Coordinated [type of project/deliverable] for [government client] with [number] stakeholders, managing review timelines and [outcome].
Briefed [audience, e.g., county officials or agency staff] on [preparedness/recovery policy topic], translating complex requirements into clear recommendations.
Managed [number] concurrent [plans/applications/reports] in a fast-paced environment, meeting [deadline or quality standard].
interview_questions: Walk us through how you would manage a rezoning application from submission to Board of Supervisors hearing.
Tell us about a time you handled conflicting stakeholder interests, such as residents opposing a project.
How would you explain a staff recommendation to an elected official who disagrees with it?
What land use issues do you see facing Loudoun County right now?
watch_outs: You may not meet the minimum qualifications if a planning degree or substantial land use experience is required.
The closing date is not stated, so the posting could close without notice.
The role includes leading teams, and the posting does not say whether prior supervisory or planning leadership experience is expected.
The salary range is wide, so a newcomer to planning should expect an offer near the bottom.
